newsitem.title: PERU: Explosion heard at besieged Japanese embassy in Peru.
newsitem.headline: Explosion heard at besieged Japanese embassy in Peru.

text.p: A loud explosion was heard early on Thursday from the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima, where Marxist rebels were holding 104 VIP hostages, officials said.
"The explosion came from within the residence at the back part. We are trying to investigate it but we cannot get very close," Nestor Ramos, a police officer at the site, said.
It was not clear whether the explosion came from inside the building or the grounds of the residence.
Witnesses said that before the explosion -- heard at around 1:45 A.M. local time (0645 GMT) -- they saw no unusual movement of police guarding the site.
The explosion was immediately followed by silence from within the residence, police and eyewitnesses said.
There were no immediate reports of injuries and television images showed no obvious damage to the building.
An unidentified policeman told the CPN local radio station that the explosion sounded as if it had the strength of no more than four sticks of dynamite.
Local television, which has been transmitting live pictures of the inside of the compound during the nine-day siege, reported no movement was seen in the compound or the residence's building.
One television station reported seeing two men running away from the residence compound over nearby roofs shortly after the explosion. This could not be confirmed.
Immediately following the explosion, police instructed the media to take cover and turn off their camera lights but allowed them to be turned on again a few minutes later, witnesses said.
The residence has been under siege since last Tuesday when about 20 heavily-armed Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels stormed the residence.
The MRTA rebels were holding hostages, including government officials, Japanese VIPs and some foreign diplomats.

In the ninth day of the siege, the rebels and the Peruvian government were deadlocked over the guerrilla demand that their jailed comrades be released -- a demand President Alberto Fujimori has refused to consider.

Since the initial assault on the residence, in separate incidents, one single shot and a loud explosion have been heard from within the embassy compound. Each of these events passed without injuries, according to the Red Cross.
